implementation_policy: Do not implement product changes from this artifact without an explicit implementation request.

north_star.goal: Awidat should become an agent editor that can produce technically clean, intentional, professional-quality edits for users who are not professional editors.
north_star.non_goal: Do not clone Resolve, Premiere, or Final Cut as interfaces. Use them to identify professional editing substrate and decision coverage.
north_star.sequencing: Build professional editing substrate first. The autonomous decision layer comes after agents can reliably inspect, plan, mutate, review, and deliver across the full pipeline.

edl_ops.summary: Typed EDL operations already cover trim, delete, split, untrim, insert, b-roll, PiP, move, transition, cut intent, audio lead/trail, track audio, ducking, sync groups, audio FX, generic effects, speed, color correction, LUTs, titles, captions, output format, loudness, package metadata, and broadcast overlays.

awidat_metadata.summary: Timeline and clip metadata already preserve source assets, anchors, hard-cut semantic intent, split edits, broadcast overlay config, and forward-compatible extra fields.

desktop_protocol.summary: Desktop protocol exposes proposed edits, timeline snapshots, cut boundaries, preview limitations, track audio controls, clip effects, titles, overlays, transitions, and editorial notes.

effect_registry.summary: Stable graph-native effect ids exist for volume, speed, color correction, LUT, title, video overlay, audio fade, and audio FX.

indexers.summary: Bundled indexers include audio energy, scene detection, Whisper, topic, editorial moments, CLIP, face, shot, gaze, frame quality, color analysis, and composition.

desktop_surface.summary: Desktop has chat, transcript, edit history, media preview, timeline, properties, notes, proposal approval, import, indexing, export, and permission modes.

skills.summary: Bundled skills already cover rough assembly, cut direction, split edits, transitions, b-roll, thematic montage, color correction, podcast editing, short-form, tutorials, beat sync, and version control.

substrate_principles: Agent tools are the primary product surface. Manual controls exist where they improve review, correction, trust, or expert override.
Every professional operation should have a durable data representation before it has a large manual UI.
Evidence, intent, and review state must persist with edits so future agents can explain and revise work.
Render and preview parity should be explicit. Known gaps should produce preview limitation or preflight findings instead of silent mismatch.
Use small, serializable, diffable contracts for substrate. Avoid opaque generated filter graphs in project metadata.

implementation_phases.name: Foundation: asset catalog, selects, delivery profile skeleton
implementation_phases.rationale: Professional work starts before the timeline. Agents need organized source assets, range-level selects, and delivery constraints before they can assemble or finish reliably.
exit_criteria: Agents can query assets by bin, role, tag, readiness, and evidence state.
Selects and stringouts persist independently from timeline clips.
At least one delivery profile can be selected and validated before render.

implementation_phases.name: Assembly and direct editing substrate
implementation_phases.rationale: Awidat already has broad EDL primitives, but professional correction and trust need richer timeline semantics and review lenses.
exit_criteria: Ripple, roll, slip, slide, lift, extract, replace, append, overwrite, markers, and ranges have typed operations or explicit non-support decisions.
Assembly proposals can be reviewed separately from finishing proposals.
Every proposal can carry evidence and intent.

implementation_phases.name: Keyframes and reusable motion graphics
implementation_phases.rationale: Professional polish depends on animated parameters and reusable graphics, not only static title overlays.
exit_criteria: A general keyframe schema exists and is renderable for a small set of high-value parameters.
Templates are serializable, diffable, previewable, and fillable by agents.
Preview limitations are explicit when animation cannot be represented exactly.

implementation_phases.name: Tracking, masks, mattes, and composition graph
implementation_phases.rationale: Tracked overlays, invisible fixes, masks, and compositing need evidence contracts before any large node UI or advanced autonomous VFX behavior.
exit_criteria: Tracks, masks, and mattes can be stored as sidecars with confidence and review artifacts.
A small composition graph can bind media, transform, merge, mask, text, and output nodes.
Agents can propose tracked inserts and mask-bound effects with reviewable quality checks.

implementation_phases.name: Color, audio, and delivery finishing workflows
implementation_phases.rationale: Finishing must be reviewable as workflows, not only as clip-level knobs.
exit_criteria: Color match uses reference stills, shot groups, grade stages, and review packs.
Audio mix uses roles, buses, meters, automation, loudness checks, and audition packs.
Delivery has queueing, preflight, post-render validation, and package manifests.

implementation_phases.name: Autonomy readiness contracts
implementation_phases.rationale: Only after substrate exists should Awidat build the broad autonomous editor brain. This phase defines the readiness API the decision layer will orchestrate.
exit_criteria: A pipeline readiness report can state which stages are available, incomplete, or blocked.
The agent can plan multi-pass edits across media, selects, assembly, VFX, color, audio, and delivery using typed substrate.
Accepted and rejected proposals produce learnable signals without requiring user knowledge of editing terminology.

build_first_recommendation: Start with phase_1_foundation_catalog_selects because it unlocks durable source organization, selection state, and delivery constraints.
Do not start with the autonomous decision layer. It would have to infer missing catalog, select, keyframe, tracking, color, audio, and delivery state from weak proxies.
Keep manual UI thin at first: status browsers, review packs, and correction controls. Put most new capability behind typed agent tools and proposal artifacts.
defer_until_substrate_exists: Opaque generated FFmpeg graphs in project metadata
Advanced 3D/particle systems before basic graph, track, mask, and keyframe contracts
